AbstractText.Label: BACKGROUND
AbstractText.content: The aim of this study was to examine the association between early menarche (<12 years) and non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) in premenopausal women and to explore whether it is mediated by adult obesity and insulin resistance.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: We analyzed data of premenopausal women, aged 15 or older, from the Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (2007-2009). We divided the women into 3 groups: early menarche, reference (12.00-15.99 years), and late menarche. The presence of NAFLD was determined using hepatic steatosis index over 36.0.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: Of the 4387 women evaluated, 673 (15.4%) subjects fit the criteria for NAFLD. The prevalence of NAFLD were higher in both women with early and late menarche compared with reference (early, 23.4%; reference, 14.0%; late, 19.9%, P <0.001). After adjustment of confounders including age, the OR for NAFLD in early menarche comparing the reference was 3.04(95% CIs: 1.99 4.65). Further adjustment of mediators, like central obesity or insulin resistance, attenuates the association to 1.91 and 2.17, but significant. However, there was no association between late menarche and NAFLD after adjustment of confounders.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: Early menarche was associated with an increased risk of NAFLD in young and middle aged premenopausal Korean women. This article is protected by copyright. All rights reserved.
